aspects.says: Code finds the multiplexer by name in the JVM that runs Q2 each time it uses it; a kept reference stops receiving answers after a redeploy.
basis: section:1.5 Your Code Finds the Multiplexer by Name, Inside Q2's JVM, When It Needs It
section:1.5.1 Spot the Problem: The Cached Multiplexer

aspects.says: ProtectedLogListener masks the log event only for the listeners listed after it, and never changes the message that is sent.
basis: section:1.6 The Log Is Masked Before Anything Writes It

aspects.says: request returns null when no answer comes in time, and on a dead link it queues the message and waits, so a client checks isConnected() first to tell a down link from a silent host.
basis: section:1.4 `request` Returns `null` When Nothing Comes Back

aspects.says: A ${name:default} value in a descriptor comes from the environment, a system property or cfg/default.yml, and the default only when all are missing.
basis: section:1.2 The Channel and the Multiplexer Share Only Two Queues, and the Queues Cross
aspects.reason: the lookup order is observed only by starting Q2 with different environments, which a graded offline run does not do; the page shows the three runs

aspects.says: Q2 creates, starts and stops the client's components from the files in deploy/, in file-name order, and replaces a component with a new object when its file changes.
basis: section:1.1 Q2 Builds the Client From the Files in `deploy/`

aspects.says: The multiplexer writes requests to the queue the adaptor reads and reads the queue the adaptor writes; with the names copied instead of crossed, every request waits out its timeout and the host sees nothing.
basis: section:1.2 The Channel and the Multiplexer Share Only Two Queues, and the Queues Cross

aspects.says: isConnected() looks only for the ready entry named in <ready>, the adaptor's name plus .ready; without it a dead link reports connected.
basis: section:1.3 `isConnected()` Knows About the Link Only Through `<ready>`

aspects.says: A Spring application only starts and stops Q2 as a lifecycle bean; services look the multiplexer up when called, because a constructor lookup runs before Q2 has started.
basis: section:1.5.2 Spring Starts and Stops Q2, and Nothing Else

aspects.says: The course runs on jPOS 2.1.7, Java 17 and Maven; 2.1.x is the maintenance line and jPOS is AGPL v3 with a commercial licence.
basis: section:1.1 Q2 Builds the Client From the Files in `deploy/`
